headline: Profit rises as merger synergies land, credit holds steady
summary_short: Net income rose to $208M, up 8.3% q/q and 36.5% y/y, as diluted EPS of $0.73 held flat y/y against a 36.4% larger diluted share count from the Pacific Premier acquisition; NIM held near 3.93% and credit costs stayed contained.
summary_long: Net income was $208M (+8.3% q/q, +36.5% y/y); diluted EPS $0.73 was flat y/y as the Pacific Premier deal lifted diluted shares 36.4% to 286.5M. NII fell $5M q/q to $589M as NIM slipped 3bp to 3.93%, mostly interest-income reversals, not core repricing. Non-interest expense fell $19M q/q on lower merger costs as cost synergies completed. Credit quality improved: charge-offs eased to 0.25% of average loans, provision held at $27M. Cash fell to $1.77B (-15.7% q/q) on planned brokered-deposit runoff; the company repurchased $199M of stock and paid a $0.37 dividend. No new numeric guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Growth reflects lower non-interest expense (merger costs down $19M q/q) and higher non-interest income, partially offset by a $5M net-interest-income decline from rate reversals and balance-sheet deleveraging.
Y/y EPS held flat as net income rose 36.5% but diluted share count grew 36.4% from shares issued in the Pacific Premier acquisition, diluting per-share gains.
Cash and equivalents fell to $1.77B on planned balance-sheet optimization; total available liquidity remained $25.6B (39% of assets) including off-balance-sheet lines.
Equity fell q/q as $199M of buybacks and dividends exceeded net income growth, and AOCI widened to $(310)M on higher unrealized securities losses.
Share count jumped 36% y/y from shares issued in the Pacific Premier acquisition (closed August 2025); q/q count fell 1.9% on $199M of buybacks reducing shares outstanding.

Management called results a reflection of disciplined execution, citing commercial loan growth, completed Pacific Premier cost synergies, and continued balance-sheet optimization; no numeric guidance was issued for future periods.
